subject: Private VPC decision follow-up — peering vs PrivateLink and egress IPs
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wong <emma.wong@sentryhealth.com>, SentryHealth NetOps <netops@sentryhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-07-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private VPC decision follow-up — peering vs PrivateLink and egress IPs

Hi Emma / NetOps team,

Thanks again for the call this morning — good discussion and appreciated the level of detail on your compliance constraints. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment: 

Summary of what SentryHealth needs (from today's conversation):
- Data residency + auditability: private connectivity option (VPC peering or PrivateLink) to avoid public internet paths.
- Static egress IPs for allowlisting outbound requests to third-party services.
- Clear owner for egress NAT (you indicated this might live in SentryHealth infra but wanted to confirm).
- KMS/HSM integration requirement for customer-managed keys (optional in first phase, required for production).
- SOC 2 evidence and network diagrams for procurement.

Deployment modes we discussed: Hosted API (fastest onboarding), Dedicated capacity (dedicated GPUs, better isolation), Private VPC (most control + compliance). From our read, Private VPC with VPC peering is likely the simplest for your NetOps team, but PrivateLink is preferred in orgs that disallow peering or need finer routing controls.

Open technical questions we need answers for to finalize the recommendation and prepare a NetOps workshop:
1) Will SentryHealth operate the NAT/egress appliance (and therefore provide the static IPs), or do you want Redwood to provide outbound egress IPs from our edge (we can provide a limited set of static egress IPs under a Dedicated/Private plan)?
2) Do you have a preferred path: VPC peering (regional, lower latency) vs AWS PrivateLink (interface endpoints) vs Transit gateway? Any policy preference?
3) Any hard constraints on ports/protocols (e.g., outbound only on 443, or allow internal health-check ports)?
4) Who will own KMS key management initially? Will you accept Redwood-managed KMS for staging?

Proposed next steps:
- NetOps deep-dive (60 min): network diagram, CIDR ranges, proposed peering connections, and allowlist exchange. Action owner: SentryHealth NetOps + Redwood NetOps (Ben).
- Provide SOC2 summary and a high level private VPC checklist (attached). Action owner: Redwood (Jonas).
- If SentryHealth prefers Redwood-provided egress IPs, we will scope IP allocation and SLA implications. Action owner: Redwood (Marissa).

Please reply inline with answers to the four questions and available times for a NetOps deep-dive next week.

Attachments: redwood-private-vpc-networking-checklist.pdf (high-level), SOC2-summary-2025.pdf (redacted).

Thanks — Jonas

--

Subject: Re: Private VPC decision follow-up — peering vs PrivateLink and egress IPs

Jonas — thanks for the recap, very helpful. Quick answers from NetOps: 

1) NAT/egress ownership: We prefer to own egress IPs for audit reasons. We'll plan to place a NAT gateway in our account and give you the static IPs to use in allowlists.
2) Preferred path: We prefer VPC peering in our initial region (us-west-2) for lower maintenance and predictable routing. We may evaluate PrivateLink for cross-account isolation later.
3) Ports/protocols: Outbound only to 443 and 5432 (we have a managed analytics sink that needs TCP 5432). Otherwise outbound HTTPs only.
4) KMS: We'll use Redwood-managed KMS for staging but require customer-managed keys (KMS in our AWS account or HSM) for production.

Follow-ups: please send the specific CIDR ranges you need on your side for peering, and a template allowlist we can copy into our ticketing system.

— SentryHealth NetOps
Netops Team | SentryHealth
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Private VPC decision follow-up — peering vs PrivateLink and egress IPs

Thanks — this is great and makes the path clear. Answers and next items below: 

1) CIDR and peering info from Redwood side: For VPC peering we'll use a /20 space for the initial staging environment and a /20 for production. Proposed Redwood CIDRs (example): 10.40.0.0/20 (staging), 10.41.0.0/20 (prod). If those overlap with anything on your side let me know.

2) Allowlist template (example lines you can paste into your ticketing system):
- Source: 10.40.0.0/20 (Redwood staging VPC)
- Source: 10.41.0.0/20 (Redwood production VPC)
- Destination: your inbound endpoint(s) over TCP 443 and TCP 5432 as discussed
- Notes: BGP not required; we will exchange VPC peering connection IDs and route table updates.

3) Egress IPs: Since you plan to own NAT, great — please provide the static egress IP(s) you will use for outbound requests to third parties and to our telemetry endpoints. If you prefer Redwood-provided egress for specific sinks we can scope that as an option (this adds a short procurement piece for Dedicated/Private pricing).

4) KMS: Staging on Redwood-managed KMS is fine. For production we'll compile a short guide for bringing your own KMS/HSM (integration points, required IAM roles, and expected handover steps).

Next steps I will take this afternoon:
- Share a concise NetOps runbook with peering steps and expected route changes (attached checklist).
- Coordinate calendar invites for a 60-minute NetOps deep-dive (Ben and Marissa to join).

Can you confirm a preferred slot for a deep-dive on either 2026-07-08 (Thu) 10:00–11:00 PT or 2026-07-09 (Fri) 09:00–10:00 PT?

Attachment references: redwood-private-vpc-networking-checklist.pdf (detailed steps)

Best — Jonas
